S82.01.needs: a signed-in AGI account (BYOK or local-only sessions show Unavailable instead)
S82.01.note: Shown in the CLI only; I did not check the web or desktop surfaces.
steps: Make sure you are signed in: run `agi login` if `agi usage` says no AGI credential.
Run `agi usage`.
Find the "Plan:" line under "Account usage".
Compare the plan name with the plan on your account (the plan names come from the tier labels, such as Free, Premium, Max, Ultra).
S82.01.where: Type `agi usage` in Terminal, or `/usage` inside an agi chat session. The first line is "Account usage", then "Plan:".

S82.02.needs: a signed-in AGI account with a subscription
S82.02.note: The code shows a reset countdown for the monthly window and a subscription status, but no explicit renewal or end date. Expected may not be fully met.
steps: Run `agi usage`.
Read the "Monthly:" line for its reset countdown ("resets in ...").
Read the "Subscription:" line for the status, such as active, trial, paused or ended.
Compare with your billing period on the account.
S82.02.where: Type `agi usage` in Terminal. Look for the "Monthly" line and the "Subscription:" line under "Account usage".

S82.03.note: The meter is text only; the code draws no bar or graphic.
steps: Run `agi usage`.
Read each window line, which shows "credits used" out of the allowance and "left", or a "% used" figure when the server sends percentages.
Compare the used amount with the plan allowance you expect.
S82.03.where: Type `agi usage` in Terminal. Look at the window lines under "Account usage": "5-hour window", "Weekly", "Monthly".

S82.04.needs: a signed-in AGI account that has used more than one model
S82.04.note: The "By model:" rows come from the server history; the flagship cap line only appears once the flagship window has usage.
steps: Run `agi usage`.
Find the "Flagship weekly" line, which appears when the flagship weekly window has usage.
Find the "By model:" heading and read the rows (up to 8), each with credits and request count.
In an agi chat session, `/usage` also shows "By model:" for the current session only.
S82.04.where: Type `agi usage` in Terminal. Look for the "By model:" section and the "Flagship weekly" line.

S82.10.needs: a signed-in AGI account that has run coding or work tasks
S82.10.note: The row names come from a fallback label table; the server may send its own labels.
steps: Run `agi usage`.
Find the heading "By product area:".
Read the rows "AGI Code" and "AGI Work" (with "Chat", "Deep Research", "Browser" and "Not attributed" too), each with credits and request count.
Compare the "AGI Code" and "AGI Work" amounts with the work you did.
S82.10.where: Type `agi usage` in Terminal. Look for the "By product area:" section.

S82.13.needs: a signed-in AGI account (a purchased balance needs credits bought)
S82.13.note: If the server reports only percentages, the line reads "Credits: not reported by this server" instead.
steps: Run `agi usage`.
Read each window line for "credits used" and "left", such as "Weekly" or "Monthly".
Read the "Purchased credits:" line for the purchased balance.
Compare the "left" numbers with what the account shows.
S82.13.where: Type `agi usage` in Terminal. Look at the window lines and the "Purchased credits:" line under "Account usage".

S82.14.needs: a signed-in AGI account; a purchased balance needs credits bought
steps: Run `agi usage`.
Read the plan window lines ("5-hour window", "Weekly", "Monthly", "Flagship weekly") which come from the plan allowance.
Read the separate "Purchased credits:" line, which shows the balance and "overage on" or "overage off".
Check that the purchased balance is listed apart from the plan allowance.
S82.14.where: Type `agi usage` in Terminal. Compare the window lines with the "Purchased credits:" line.

S82.17.needs: a signed-in AGI account with a window that has a reset time
steps: Run `agi usage`.
Read the window lines for ", resets in ..." (for example "resets in 3h 0m").
If the reset time has passed, the line shows "resetting now".
Compare the countdown with a clock after a minute.
S82.17.where: Type `agi usage` in Terminal. Look at the reset text on each window line.

S82.20.note: No per-task usage view found. I searched apps/cli/src for "task" with usage and cost words (for example per-task, by task, task cost) and found nothing in the usage or cost code. The usage view is per window, per model and per product area only.

S82.23.needs: a signed-in AGI account on the managed route (a BYOK or local session shows a "cost:" line instead)
S82.23.note: The "billed:" line may say "not settled yet" while settlement is pending; the code polls for up to about 3.5 seconds.
steps: Sign in with `agi login` and start a chat with `agi`.
Send one short message and wait for the answer to finish.
Look for a line starting with "billed:" below the answer (it may take a few seconds to settle).
Compare the amount with `agi usage` afterward.
S82.23.where: Start an agi chat session by typing `agi`, send a message, and look after the answer for the "billed:" line.

labels.text: Run `agi usage` to see what is left.

S82.24.needs: a signed-in AGI account near a usage limit (hard to reach in a test)
S82.24.note: The notice appears only when the server sends a quota header; I could not find a command that forces it.
steps: Sign in and use `agi` chat until a usage window reaches a warning level.
Look for the notice "You have used N% of your ..." with the window name.
The notice appears once per window and level.
Run `agi usage` and compare the percentage.
S82.24.where: Shown as a notice in an agi chat session when the server reports a window at a high usage level: "You have used N% of your 5-hour window."

labels.text: Add credits or fix billing at

S82.25.needs: a signed-in AGI account at a usage limit (hard to reach in a test)
S82.25.note: Expected mentions naming the limit, but the text names only the reset time and the recovery link. Code moved: errors.rs:373 no longer holds the quote; the usage limit text is at errors.rs:687-705.
steps: Use an account that has reached a limit (for example a flagship weekly limit).
Send a message in `agi` chat that the limit blocks.
Read the error text: it names the limit, the "It resets in" time and the recovery link ("Add credits or fix billing at" or "See every usage window at").
Compare with `agi usage`.
S82.25.where: Shown as the error text in an agi chat when a limit blocks a message, after the "It resets in ..." sentence, then the recovery link sentence.

S82.26.needs: a signed-in AGI account at the flagship weekly limit (hard to reach in a test)
S82.26.note: The alternative is offered only for the flagship weekly limit; the other limit codes give no alternative. The "Switch to" line is for an unavailable model, not a limit.
steps: Use an account at the flagship weekly limit with a model from that limit.
Send a message in `agi` chat.
Read the error text for "Your plan also includes" with a standard model name.
Type the suggested `/model <name>` and send a message to check it runs.
S82.26.where: Shown in the error text of an agi chat when the flagship weekly limit blocks a message: "Your plan also includes ..., switch with `/model ...`".

S82.27.note: No wait-until-reset option found. I searched apps/cli/src for "wait until", "until the reset" and "Wait": the limit text only says "It resets in ..." and "Run `agi usage` to see when it resets." in apps/cli/src/errors.rs.
